dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: #This place is great — so quiet and serene, like nothing could ever threaten the peace. I admire what you've accomplished here, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I hope Natlan enjoys a similar tranquility one day.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you like it here?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: It's great! It feels like a vacation spot, almost like the People of the Springs.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Before I became Pyro Archon, I went to the hot springs all the time. It's the perfect place to unwind and meet people from all walks of life, outlanders included.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: But, that kind of free time is few and far between these days.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You could always try to find that old feeling again.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Hahaha, I actually prefer to keep busy. Let me put it this way...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I'm sure you've invited many friends here in the past. And like me, they probably walked away with a very positive impression of this place.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: From the environment to the decorations, you planned out everything down to the smallest detail.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Behind everything we see here lies a tremendous amount of work. And, you do that work, because this is your home, right?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Collecting ingredients, crafting furnishings, planning the layout and design... I'm sure all of that kept you very busy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, but it was very fulfilling.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Exactly. That's how I feel about Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Some bear their responsibilities like a burden, out of a sense of identity or obligation. But, I have a vision, and that is what drives me forward.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The role of "Pyro Archon" simply makes it easier for me to fulfill that vision.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Hehe, that comes as no surprise to me. You're someone with a clear set of morals — through all the trials and tribulations, your resolve never wavered.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: That conviction is one of the key qualities of a leader.

choices.text: Hmm, can't say I really get it...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: It's alright, that's just my own take on things.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Based on what I've seen, you have your own understanding of the world, and your place in it, so just believe in yourself — you're on the right path.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to have a chat with me?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Oh, sure. I took some time to walk around this place and came up with a few suggestions. Maybe you'll get some inspiration...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Ah, from the look on your face, you were hoping for a more... casual conversation. Haha, that's very valid. My apologies — I can never seem to stop working.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You remind me of some of my other friends...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Let me guess — they also have high standards for themselves and their surroundings.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Of course, not everyone's like that, and I respect other people's choices. So, I try to operate without imposing my habits on anyone else.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: We're all human, which means we're often at the mercy of our emotions. When we get tired or annoyed, we lose focus, and it's hard to be efficient.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: No matter how urgent or important, in that situation, it's better to put the work aside and get some rest.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: True... But there are also times when you just want to power through.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: You're not wrong. I used to think some people were just built that way — so conscientious by nature that they just can't tear themselves away from their work.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: But eventually, I realized it's not a character trait at all, but a reaction that stems from prolonged periods of anxiety and stress.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: There are many possible factors — lack of recognition, family issues, disrupted sleep, lack of exercise...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I try to ensure that we have enough manpower at our disposal so everyone can afford to take breaks. The shamans from the Masters of the Night-Wind can also help relieve stress.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Thankfully, I'm quite the workaholic, so even if a lot of people go on break at once, it's all the same to me, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What if people would take advantage of that to be lazy?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Well, that depends on the context. I don't view it as some kind of inherent evil. It's a choice.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: All I need to know is whether someone is driven by the same vision... Of course, actions speak louder than words in that regard.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I can talk with them, offer suggestions, and guide their next steps. There will always be things I don't understand, but as the Pyro Archon, I can still help people find the right path forward.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: But, first and foremost, they have to be willing. And, that is not a decision I can make for them.

choices.text: It seems like you really respect everyone.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Hehe, I wouldn't go that far. I just don't want everyone to turn into a workaholic like me. After all, that lifestyle's not for everyone.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Plus, it leads to a more relaxed atmosphere, which is better for everyone, don't you think?

choices.text: That feels a bit... over-idealized to me?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Well, we're talking about principles. In a vacuum, I'm sure it sounds vague and impractical. But in practice, there are a variety of factors I consider.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Still, I won't refute your assessment. I consider myself an idealist, after all.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: In my experience, surrounding yourself with people who share a common ideal... can be a very powerful thing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anything you'd like to do?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Well, since you asked, I have an idea for a flamestrider Grand Prix!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wh—What was that?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Hahaha, I've been thinking about it ever since I arrived! It would be a shame not to take advantage of all this space and the amazing scenery.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: So, this is what I was thinking... We create a race track that combines speed and technique and invite challengers to compete. The winner can be crowned the "Master of the Striding Flame."

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: If the tournament is a success, it would bring in a significant profit, in which case, you wouldn't need to worry about future prizes, and you could even expand the scale.

choices.text: I see where you're coming from, but...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Oh, don't worry. I already asked Xilonen about that. Although, she categorically refused...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I understand her reasoning, of course. I would need at least eight flamestriders, which would cost a small fortune, and I have no idea where we would find enough Secret Source components.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Still, having a vision is better than nothing. Besides, I have a back-up plan that only involves one rider.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Instead of having everyone ride a flamestrider at once, everyone will take turns with mine, and the person with the fastest time wins.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Of course, Xilonen rejected this proposal as well. The reason being, the flamestrider was originally designed for battle and travel, rather than speed.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Several modifications would need to be made to operate at high speeds, which means faster wear and tear, and more maintenance.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: In short, we cannot sacrifice the core function of the flamestrider for our own entertainment.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Xilonen makes a convincing argument...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Hm... True.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: But, that also means... We could just design a new flamestrider built entirely for speed!

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I'll make a quick sketch and show it to Xilonen right away!

choices.text: Do you have enough flamestriders for that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning, Mavuika.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Morning! Another busy day lies ahead, and I'm ready to tackle it head-on.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night, Mavuika.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Ah, good night. I was just doing some puzzles — it's a collection from the Akademiya in Sumeru. I'll call it a night after these last two problems.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Did you set up this office just for me? Aw. That's so nice of you.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Whenever I need space to think, I pace around in the Speaker's Chamber and before I realize it, I find myself tinkering with the furnishings. Or doing even weirder things.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: For example, I might wipe down the lampshade of the phlogiston lamp several times over, or start cantering around on the wooden alpaca carving... It actually works, okay? Don't knock it till you've tried it.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: This makes me imagine a huge feast... Everyone raising their glasses, enjoying some good food, and letting their hair down.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: We've got the venue, we've got the feast... All that's missing is a bit of healthy competition.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: To have a proper feast, you need a reason to celebrate — just like you can't have drinks without some snacks. That's what sets the mood, and allows everyone to fully enjoy themselves.
